Workshop on Advancing Wind Farm Flow Control through Sensors and Algorithms

On October 14 and 15, the IEA Wind Task 44/Task 52 Workshop on “Advancing Wind Farm Flow Control through Sensors and Algorithms” took place at the Goldwind Science & Technology Park in Beijing. Around 30 participants from Europe, America and Asia attended in person and more than 30 participants joined online. Workshop participants presented the latest research results, industrial needs and challenges related to optimizing wind farm operation and discussed opportunities for improving wind farm flow control using sensors and algorithms.

Background

Wind farm flow control is a control strategy in which individual wind turbines are controlled to achieve plant-level objectives, such as increasing energy production or reducing structural loads, by mitigating the impact of wake interactions. Although commercial adoption of wind farm flow control (e.g., wake steering) is growing, determining the most effective use of sensors and algorithms for maximizing the benefits of the technology is still an active area of research.

The aim of this workshop is to combine the experience of wind farm owners and the wind farm control and wind energy sensor communities to identify how sensors and algorithms can be used to improve the performance of wind farm flow control. Although lidars are one of the most widely deployed types of wind sensors in the wind industry, a wide variety of sensors will be considered in the workshop, including lidar, radar, nacelle instrumentation, blade sensors, pressure sensors, sound emission sensors, and more. Further, algorithms that use the measurements from these sensors to improve wind farm flow control performance will be discussed as well.

Objective




The objectives of the workshop are to bring together researchers and industry experts to address the following questions:



What are the challenges and needs for wind farm operation?

What information is needed to improve the effectiveness of wind farm control?

What are the capabilities and experience with available sensors and algorithms for wind farm control?

How can we improve sensors and algorithms for wind farm control?
